summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-18 (window Oct. 12–18). My search capacity ran out partway through, so I'm submitting two candidates, not four. Both are institutional election blunders, and I opened and checked the pages and quotes for each. 1) Maryland's state elections board said Anne Arundel County mailed sample ballots that were missing their last two pages. Three accepted outlets cover it (CBS Baltimore, WMAR-2, FOX45). 2) Texas's Secretary of State's office told counties about a second state error that had held back about 15,000 voter address updates, four days before early voting. Sources are Votebeat/Texas Tribune and KERA. Several other leads were set aside, mostly because they had no accepted source. Genius: Scan for 2026-10-18 (GENIUS; window Oct. 12–18). The search budget ran out early, so most of the work went into opening ScienceDaily, Nature news and NASA pages that had already turned up. One candidate holds up: on Oct. 14, NASA reported that the Roman Space Telescope's Wide Field Instrument, after being aligned by a Goddard team, beats its predicted image quality by nearly 30%. NASA's own page plus ScienceDaily make a complete pair. Most other leads were led from outside the US, were journal papers published before the window and reposted later, or had only one accepted publisher. Gretchen Walsh's Oct. 16 world record still has no accepted publisher. Only one candidate is submitted. Pair published.
